sources: Python datetime module: aware and naive datetime objects

defects.class: offset of an ISO-8601 expiry string dropped by replace(tzinfo=None) before comparing with naive UTC time
defects.description: Line 53 `expires_at = datetime.fromisoformat(token.expires_at).replace(tzinfo=None)` keeps the wall-clock time of the identity-provider string and discards its UTC offset. Input: token.expires_at = "2026-10-17T09:30:00+02:00" (expiry instant 07:30 UTC) and now = datetime(2026, 10, 17, 8, 0) (naive UTC, 08:00 UTC). Wrong result: is_expired returns False (compares 08:00 with 09:30) and store.get returns the token. Expected result: is_expired returns True because 08:00 UTC is at or after 07:30 UTC. The token stays valid for the offset length (2 hours here) after its real expiry. No exception is raised, so the error is silent.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Both arguments are converted with astimezone(timezone.utc) before subtraction, so the difference is computed on the same UTC basis regardless of their offsets. seconds_until(datetime(2026,10,17,9,30,tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=2))), datetime(2026,10,17,8,0,tzinfo=timezone.utc)) = -1800 (09:30+02:00 is 07:30 UTC, which is 30 minutes before 08:00 UTC). It handles the offset correctly, as the intent requires; the docstring states the aware-input contract. seconds_until has no caller in this case; it is a dead helper and is not part of the keyed defect.

Unchanged base function is_idle_expired. Both now (default from naive_utc_now()) and token.last_seen (set by new_token() and get() via naive_utc_now()) are naive UTC values created by the same helper, so the subtraction and comparison are consistent. It looks like a naive/aware mix but is correct. It is an unchanged line in base and outside the added code (it appears only as a context line of the hunk), and must not be reported in diff mode.
